2026-11-08-body-01.description:
One magnet usually passes, but two or more can pull together through your gut walls, and on an X-ray they can look like just one. If a magnet is swallowed, see a doctor right away (US Poison Control: 1-800-222-1222).
Next Body File: what happens if you hold your pee until your bladder balloons.

2026-11-09-body-02.description:
About 9 in 10 people struck by lightning survive, and the fern-like Lichtenberg figures some get are not burns: they fade within hours. If someone is struck, they're safe to touch, so call 911 and start CPR.

2026-11-09-body-03.description:
Drinking about a gallon of water in an hour or two can dilute your blood sodium, so water moves into your cells and they swell, including in your brain. It's rare, and drinking water is vital: drink when you're thirsty.

2026-11-09-body-04.topic_source: backlog #1: mandatory next_topic_must_be, promised by the water video (2026-11-09-body-3) with the 'what's really making that pop' tease (paid off in lines 3-7)
2026-11-09-body-04.description:
The pop is gas in the fluid that lubricates your finger joints, and it needs time to build back up before that knuckle cracks again. Studies, including one doctor who cracked only his left hand for about 50 years, found no link to arthritis. If it hurts or swells, see a doctor.
